default.$description: Primary button fill — a lightened brand. Button-only gimmick: color.text.brand / color.icon.brand stay at 600 everywhere else.
Glass catch on the coloured primary surface — hand-tuned, not on the palette.

active.$description: Full 1.5px white border on focus / active — high contrast on the brand fill (parallels color.button.secondary.border.active).

default.$description: Inner-shadow colour for the 'Viginette primary 2xs' effect style (hand-tuned).
Same glass surface as Card / StatButton — #fcfcfc, unchanged by state (hover swaps the shadow, not the fill).
White glass catch (top + left) at rest / hover.

active.$description: Full 1.5px primary border on focus / active.

default.$description: Text-only button — same colour as the secondary label at rest; hover adds an underline.

hover.$description: Reserved — for the future interactive-card hover state (not used yet)

border.$description: The asymmetric glass catch (top + left, 1.5px, white). Widths + the inner-shadow are hand-tuned in the CSS, not tokens.

border-active.$description: Focused/active glass border — full 1.5px primary, replaces the white top-left catch. Shared by Card, StatButton, and other glass buttons.

badge.$description: Redesigned to a glass recipe (2026-09-16): a radial highlight glow + a colored inner shadow, both hand-tuned per tone off each tone's own primitive ramp — no flat `background` fill anymore, so that key is gone from every tone below. `glow`/`shadow` are a deliberate primitive-alias exception (same treatment as `table.row.background.danger/success`): there's no existing semantic role at the 300/400 prominence step these need, and the recipe is a per-component visual effect (like `button.primary.shadow`), not a general-purpose color decision. `text` is *also* now a deliberate primitive alias for all 6 tones, not just warning's pre-existing one below — each badge's label (and its optional leading icon, which reuses this same token) reads better one step lighter (600) than the shared semantic text.<tone> (which sits at 700, calibrated for body text elsewhere), consistent with the rationale warning's exception already documented.

shadow.$description: One step darker than glow — neutral has no hue to lean on, so the inner shadow needs the extra step to read as depth rather than just a flat gray smear.
One step darker than glow, same reasoning as neutral.shadow — brand kept the asymmetric pair rather than being flattened to match the other 4 tones.
Same step as glow — unlike neutral/brand, success/warning/danger/warning-strong reuse one shade for both, since their own hue already carries enough depth without a darker second step.

text.$description: One step lighter than text.warning (amber.700) — deliberate primitive alias so the amber `warning` badge is clearly distinct from the orange `warning-strong` badge. Small contrast tradeoff (~3.2:1) accepted for level differentiation.

info.$description: Untouched by the 2026-09-16 glass redesign above — `info` has no matching Figma variant on the Badge component (a pre-existing code-only tone), so there's no glass recipe to port for it yet. Still the old flat background/text shape.

default.$description: zinc.100. Owner decided the header row only ever needs one flat color — no separate active/focused state — so this took over the value that had briefly been header.background.active; the original default (color.surface.subtle, zinc.50) was removed since it's no longer used anywhere.

Fixed from color.surface.default (#ffffff) — rows/cells sit directly on Table's own Card-replica surface (#fcfcfc via color.card.background.default), not as a separate white panel. TableCell itself is transparent; TableRow is what actually carries this fill.

active.$description: Focused row — mirrors row.background.default exactly (owner's call: the fill doesn't change on focus, only the border does — same restraint Input uses for its own focus state). Aliased to the token, not duplicated, so it can never drift from default.

danger.$description: Deliberate primitive alias, one step paler than color.background.danger-subtle (rose.100) — owner's explicit choice for a low-contrast row wash, not the louder banner-style danger-subtle tone.

success.$description: Deliberate primitive alias, one step paler than color.background.success-subtle (emerald.100) — same reasoning as row.background.danger.

active.$description: 1px focus ring around the whole row — the only visible signal for the active/focused state now that its background mirrors default. Same token Input uses for its own focus border.

hover.$description: Inset shadow, not a fill — the row has no background by default, hover darkens via an inner-shadow wash instead of swapping a fill. Shared with scrollableArea.row.shadow.hover.

background.$description: Recessed/inset scroll track, same intent as other inset zones

shadow.$description: Inner-shadow tint at the scroll edges. Was a raw #00000026 before the alpha-black primitive ramp existed — now a proper alias, same value (15%).

hover.$description: Inset shadow, not a fill — rows have no background by default. Shared with table.row.shadow.hover.

focus.$description: 1px inset border for keyboard focus — inset (box-shadow, not outline) to stay consistent with the row's own no-fill, inset-shadow-hover treatment instead of an outer glow.

divider.$description: Permanent 1px bottom-only divider between rows in a list — every state (default/hover/focus), unlike hover/focus which only apply on interaction. Owner changed this from border.subtle (zinc.100, "faint separators") to border.default (zinc.200, "inputs, cards, dividers") directly in Figma — a plain divider apparently read as too faint at subtle. CSS: box-shadow inset (layout-neutral, stacks with the focus ring as a second shadow layer). Figma: a real per-side stroke (strokeBottomWeight 1, others 0, INSIDE align, strokesIncludedInLayout false) — NOT an effect. An INNER_SHADOW effect on this frame (which has no fill) was confirmed to corrupt Figma's own text rendering for this file's variable-font weight; a stroke on the same no-fill frame does not. See docs/components/Row.md and HANDOFF.md §6.

off.$description: zinc.100, "wells, code blocks, inset track" — literally the inset-track description this token already carries, reused verbatim for the off-state track.

on.$description: brand.600, same token Button primary/selected-state uses.

thumb.$description: Always a plain white circle regardless of track state — the track color alone carries on/off/disabled.

disabled.$description: Same value as background.disabled (zinc.100) — a disabled checkbox reads as one flat muted shape, no separate border needed to stand out.

focus.$description: Added when Checkbox adopted a real focus variant (the previous 3-state default/hover/disabled set never modeled one) — same token Input/TableRow use for their own focus border.

default.$description: The checkmark (checked) / dash (indeterminate) glyph — white against the brand fill. Was a flat `checkbox.icon` leaf before React needed a disabled variant; the Figma master (4182:3616) still binds its glyph vectors to the old flat `color/checkbox/icon` name for every state, disabled included — a real Figma↔code drift, not fixed here (bridge is read-only for this task). Worth a follow-up: rename the Figma variable to `color/checkbox/icon/default` and add a sibling `color/checkbox/icon/disabled` bound onto the disabled+checked/indeterminate master variants.

disabled.$description: Same restraint as `radio.dot.disabled` — a disabled control's glyph reads as muted gray, not a bright white mark on a pale gray fill (which would be nearly invisible). Not yet reflected in the Figma master, see `default`'s note.

background.$description: Radio keeps a plain white fill in every state, checked included — unlike Checkbox, which fills solid. The dot (see below) is what signals checked, not the fill.

icon.$description: Leading/trailing icon color — always subtle, doesn't change with border state (hover/focus/error don't recolor it).

affix.$description: Prepend/append text color (e.g. a fixed unit or protocol prefix inside the field) — a subtle, non-editable annotation next to the value, not the value's own text color.

label.$description: The Label component's per-instance text color — a plain, colorable inline text bit (sentence-case, not uppercase like Tag). Just aliases the semantic text ramp; no new values. The divider between labels in a LabelGroup is NOT one of these — it's fixed chrome (color.text.subtle).

default.$description: The headline above the field, at rest — matches Row's own heading color (a field label reads as a subheading, not a page heading).

helperText.$description: The icon+message row a FormField shows below its control in a non-default state. Two tones only for now — primary (an informational note) and error (validation failure) — deliberately no 'default' entry since HelperText never renders in the default state.

background.$description: zinc.100 — the recessed track the pill items sit in.

hover.$description: Same alpha-black wash MenuRow/Row/TableRow already use for hover — a flat background here (not an inset shadow), since an unselected item has no fill of its own to layer over.

xs.$description: The xs size's own unselected recipe (2026-09-18) — introduced for the sidebar module switcher, where the item's own glass fill/border/inner-shadow/overlay (zinc + alpha-black, not the shared item.background.hover alpha-wash above) carries the unselected look regardless of tone, since tone only ever colors the `selected` state. Deliberate primitive-alias exception, same reasoning as `sidebar.navItem.hover`. `fill`/`border`/`innerShadow` step one lighter on hover (400 vs 500, everywhere at once); `overlay` instead steps UP in opacity (alpha-black.15 -> .25) — owner's follow-up tweak once the 400-step recipe was in place, making hover read as a firmer press rather than just a paler tint.

progressBar.$description: Striped-fill redesign (2026-09-16), revised same day: the fill is its own bordered, shadowed pill with a diagonal line pattern of the tone's main color + a lighter tint. Owner moved the main fill one step lighter (600/500 -> 500/400 — 'more subtle') and moved `border`/`shadow` off per-tone hue.700 onto shared neutral glass tokens (a white edge highlight + a flat black-alpha shadow, matching Card's own glass vocabulary) after prototyping on one variant — `fill`/`border`/`shadow` below reflect that final state, not the original per-tone-hue.700 version. `fill`/`stripe` stay a deliberate primitive-alias exception (same treatment as `badge.<tone>.glow/shadow` — no semantic role at these exact prominence steps, and it's a per-component visual effect); `border`/`shadow` now route through real existing semantic/primitive tokens instead (`color.border.highlight`, `color.alpha-black.20`), so they're no longer primitive-tier exceptions themselves, just reuse of tokens already established for the same glass look elsewhere.

border.$description: The gray track's own 0.5px frame — plain semantic, no tone variation (the track is always neutral).
White edge highlight, not tone-colored — the same glass-catch token Card/Modal use, reused here rather than inventing a white primitive alias.

shadow.$description: Flat neutral shadow, not tone-colored — replaces the earlier per-tone hue.700 shadow.

fill.$description: One step lighter than the shared color.background.brand.default (600) — ProgressBar's own main color now diverges from that semantic token on purpose, so lightening it here never affects Button/Badge/etc.

stripe.$description: Kept at 400 (not shifted down with fill) — owner's explicit preference for a very subtle fill/stripe contrast, tighter than the original 2-step gap.

fill.$description: Owner's correction — the 500-600->400-500 ramp shift briefly landed this at amber.400, one step below the shared color.background.warning (amber.500); owner wanted warning's fill to stay at 500, unlike the other 3 tones which did shift down a step.

stripe.$description: One step below fill (500), same relative gap the other 3 tones have between their own fill and stripe — the earlier 'same as fill' note no longer applies now that fill moved back to 500.

sidebar.$description: Component-scoped exceptions from the sidebar's own design (2026-09-17), none matching an existing semantic step: `icon.default`/`text.default` are a deliberately dimmer 'on dark' than the shared icon.on-emphasis/text.on-emphasis (zinc.50) — a calmer, quieter default for a nav rail meant to recede behind the page content, not compete with it. `panel.background` sits between the shared background.emphasis (zinc.700, the sidebar's own base) and background.subtle (zinc.100) with no existing semantic step at zinc.600; `panel.innerShadow` is the matching inset-edge tint for that same panel surface, one step down at zinc.500 (replaces a raw unbound literal that was previously hand-set directly on the panel effect in Figma, not aliased to anything). `<tone>.fill`/`<tone>.accent` deliberately do NOT reuse the shared background.<tone>/text.<tone>/icon.<tone> tokens (600/700) — those steps are calibrated for tone-as-accent on a LIGHT surface; on this component's dark background they read muddy and low-contrast. 500 (fill, for the module switcher's larger solid area) and 400 (accent, for the switcher's stroke/inner-shadow and the active nav row's icon+text) are one and two steps lighter respectively, matching what actually reads clearly against color.background.emphasis. `navItem.active.*` is the active/current nav row's own recipe — a neutral glass highlight (fill/overlay/border/innerShadow, all zinc/alpha-black, matching the module switcher's unselected-item recipe) that stays tone-agnostic on purpose: only the row's icon+text recolor per module (via `<tone>.accent` above), the highlight pill itself never does. All primitive-alias exceptions, scoped to this one component.

fill.$description: Deliberately simpler than active — a flat wash with no border/inner-shadow/overlay, so hover reads as a lighter, transient touch compared to the fuller active recipe above.

mark.$description: Owner's explicit call: the logo stays pure white on the sidebar regardless of theme — not an alias into the zinc ramp like every other sidebar token above, since this one is never meant to soften or recede. Was bound to a raw color.zinc.100 in Figma before this fix (an off-white, not the intended pure white).

wordmark.$description: Same reasoning as mark, for the adjacent wordmark text — was bound to color.zinc.200 in Figma, inconsistent with the mark's own (also-wrong) near-white; both now resolve to the one correct value.

filled.$description: Completed stage points + the connecting lines between them, and the current stage's own point fill. Adopted from the owner's pre-token 'Progress bar' component (4182:3097, renamed TableProgressStages) — was bound to the old shadcn-colors 'primary/primary'.

unfilled.$description: Pending (not-yet-reached) stage points + lines. Was 'shadcn colors/general/actual muted' — same zinc.100 value, now a real semantic alias.

ring.$description: The soft halo stroke around the current/active stage's point only — every other point/line is a flat fill with no stroke. Was 'primary/bg' (a raw light-indigo shadcn variable); this system's own equivalent 'soft brand tint' token is background.brand-subtle, the same one Badge's brand tone uses.

background.$description: The one component that stays dark regardless of theme — a tooltip needs contrast against whatever's underneath, light or dark page alike.

line.$description: The standalone Divider atom's own line color. Distinct from LabelGroup's internal divider, which deliberately stays on color.text.subtle as fixed chrome — not unified, since that one predates this token and isn't worth a breaking rebind for a coincidental match.

icon.$description: A sensible static default — real usage typically recolors it via context (the same way Button's own built-in spinner adopts each variant's icon color), same restraint as an inline icon.

current.$description: The last crumb — the current page, not a link.

primary.$description: An optional brand-colored crumb — for calling out one segment of the trail (e.g. the entity type), independent of which crumb is current.

background.$description: Neutral placeholder fill behind initials — not per-user hashed color, a static reference can't model that.

ring.$description: The ring around the status dot and the action badge — separates them visually from the avatar image underneath, same idea as a real UI's cutout.

icon.$description: The add/delete glyph inside the action badge — white against either solid fill.
